Determinism check.

Pairing the ii-th model call of the adapted selector (λ=0.3\lambda=0.3) with the ii-th call of local repair in each unit (110 pairs per model): 7 (Qwen) and 4 (Mistral) pairs had byte-identical prompts and different responses; 8 and 2 later prompts differed as a consequence; the operator sets and call counts were identical in every unit.

Further results.

In all 31 memory-pipeline non-adoptions the new value was present verbatim in the use-stage prompt (Qwen 17, Mistral 14): omissions of visible current information, whose cause within the memory prompt this comparison does not isolate. No primary or secondary comparison was significant (Holm-4 and Holm-8 per model); stale commits were 0/8 in every revocation cell.

Selector behaviour.

The adapted selector at λ=0.3\lambda=0.3 selected exactly local repair’s operators in every unit (same calls; logical token totals differ by 5 and 12), a structural consequence of our value and cost definitions (minimum wi/ciw_{i}/c_{i} 4.4 and 4.2); its outputs differed only where the server returned different text for byte-identical prompts at temperature 0 (7 and 4 of 110 paired calls). At λ=10\lambda=10 it left the global summary withdrawn, saved one call per revision, and adopted 9/13 and 8/13.

Appendix N Reuse sweep (EXP-R)

Pre-specification and execution.

The sweep was run under a pre-specification plan (hashed before any model call under it) and a frozen build (the confirmatory-run build plus a repeated-use option and a model-registry entry, no scoring change). Units: the eight development screening patients of Table 5, both sizes, E1, the four pipelines and both 7B models (128 trajectories, 0 execution failures). After the E1 revision and use1 each trajectory issued 19 further medication uses (use2 to use20) with the identical use-prompt template; problem-list uses were not issued. Prompt+completion tokens per use were taken from the server usage record. One 80–96 GB data-centre GPU per model, 2,412 and 2,602 GPU-seconds. Execution amendment (dated before the jobs started): the jobs were first submitted to the default queue, cancelled before starting when the scheduler gave no start estimate, and resubmitted unchanged to a short-job queue. No selective re-run occurred.

Analysis (measured, no extrapolation).

Per patient, C⁡(k)=ingest+use0+revise+∑j≤kusejC(k)=\text{ingest}+\text{use}_{0}+\text{revise}+\sum_{j\leq k}\text{use}_{j} for the memory pipeline and for re-reading on the same patient; Δ​C​(k)\Delta C(k) is the paired difference and Fig. 5 reports the mean of the per-patient ratio Cmem​(k)/Creread​(k)C_{\mathrm{mem}}(k)/C_{\mathrm{reread}}(k) (a mean of paired ratios, not a ratio of mean costs) with a 95 % tt-interval over the eight patients. Cumulative Δ​C​(k)\Delta C(k) did not cross zero within k≤20k\leq 20 in any of the 12 cells. The mean per-use difference Umem−UrereadU_{\mathrm{mem}}-U_{\mathrm{reread}} over uses 1–20 was positive in 11 cells (+175 to +2,276 tokens) and negative in one (Mistral-7B, large, cache: −12.6-12.6 tokens per use against a fixed-cost difference Δ​I+Δ​U0+Δ​R=+8,213\Delta I+\Delta U_{0}+\Delta R=+8{,}213; the algebraic break-even 8,213/12.6≈6528{,}213/12.6\approx 652 uses is a quotient of two measured means, not an observed crossing). For the same cell the two later uses of the original screening run (Table 5) had given −57-57 tokens per use; the 20-use sweep measured −12.6-12.6. The sweep is a separate run of the same scenarios, so its ingest and use0 differ slightly from the screening run’s: its Δ​U0\Delta U_{0} for this cell is −27-27 and its fixed-cost difference 8,213, against −73-73 and 8,329 in Table 5; §6.2 quotes the sweep’s values. The local-repair later-use ratio over uses 1–20 (mean memory use tokens over mean re-reading use tokens) is 2.51, 1.91, 1.42 and 2.03 for Qwen large, Qwen small, Mistral large and Mistral small. Table 19 gives the cumulative ratios at k=1k=1, 5, 10 and 20 and the per-use differences; full per-kk values will be released with the code.

Appendix O Length sweep (EXP-X): pre-specification, amendments and full results

Pre-specification.

A plan, a frozen build, a scenario manifest (22 scenario files) and the analysis program were hashed before the first model call of the batch. The build is the reuse-sweep build plus a length-level scenario builder and the TF and RRTF use renderings; the small-scenario builder is byte-identical, so level S is the scenario of the main batches. TF maintains memory exactly as local repair does and, at use time, shows only the claims whose parent document has an allowed source, with those documents’ chunk summaries and without the global summary; RRTF is re-reading restricted to allowed-source documents. Units: the eight development screening patients of Table 5, condition E1, seed 0, one greedy decoding for every stage, and 20 later medication uses with the identical template (no problem-list use). The vLLM context limit was raised to 32,768 tokens; a serving check sent the longest XL re-reading prompt (9,825 Qwen and 10,361 Mistral tokens) twice to each model and received identical, strictly parsed answers. A level is the token count (Qwen2.5 tokenizer) of the post-revision re-reading document body, headers and small-scenario documents included. Context documents are the patient’s own records from the eICU demo tables lab, vitalperiodic, vitalaperiodic and nursecharting, one document per table and ICU day, with connector source lab or ehr; the medication task allows only pharmacy sources, so no context document can support a medication key. The intake–output table was excluded because its labels carry drug names; a scan of all 275 medication keys found none in the vital-sign tables and only analyte names (sodium, calcium, potassium, glucose) in the laboratory and nursing tables, the same collision the small scenario’s laboratory document already contains. Context documents are appended after the small documents and the revision event, so D1–D4 and the revision are byte-identical to the small scenario. They are ordered chronologically across tables (fixed table order within one ICU day) and added whole while the running total stays within the target, until it reaches 90 % of the target; the rule reads token counts only. A patient enters a level if its re-reading body lies within [0.9,1.0]×[0.9,1.0]\times the target; at S these bodies are 251–373 Qwen2.5 tokens (Mistral 276–419). XL was drafted at 12,000 tokens and set to 10,000 by the plan’s own fallback rule (the largest multiple of 1,000 reached by at least six of the eight patients). This gave 8, 3, 5 and 6 patients at S, M, L and XL; one patient is in band at all of M, L and XL, so each level is analysed on its own patients and M (n=3n=3) is descriptive.

Amendments and execution.

Two revisions were made before the plan was hashed and before any model call: the drafted fill rule, which stopped at the first document that would cross the target and reached the band for none of the eight patients at M, became the skip-and-continue rule above, and documents were ordered chronologically across tables instead of table by table, which had left fewer patients in band. After hashing, a scheduler amendment fixed explicit queue options; after the pilot job was submitted but before its projection was recorded or any batch job was submitted, a logistics amendment raised the GPU budget cap from 20 to 60 GPU-hours and moved the collection deadline. A one-patient XL pilot on Qwen (not a result; never analysed) projected 3.85 GPU-hours for the batch (about 4.1 with the serving check and the pilot), within the original cap, so the raise was not needed. Neither amendment changed the design, the scenarios or the decoding. The batch ran as eight jobs (model ×\times level): 264 trajectories, no execution failure, no duplicate and no resubmission, in 11,629 GPU-seconds (one 80–96 GB data-centre GPU per job; 12,485 with the serving check and the pilot). A seventh, optional pipeline (stateless re-extraction at every use) was declined before the freeze.

Endpoints and a disclosed omission.

Tokens are prompt plus completion from the server usage record. Per patient, the per-use difference and the per-use ratio average uses 1–20; cells report the mean over patients with a 95 % tt-interval. kobs∗k^{*}_{\mathrm{obs}} is the first k≤20k\leq 20 at which the patient-mean cumulative difference is below zero; kpred∗=(Δ​I+Δ​U0+Δ​R)/(Ureread−Umem)k^{*}_{\mathrm{pred}}=(\Delta I+\Delta U_{0}+\Delta R)/(U_{\mathrm{reread}}-U_{\mathrm{mem}}) uses the per-use difference of uses 1–3 only (0 if the pipeline is cheaper from the start). Quality endpoints use exact McNemar tests against re-reading with Holm correction over the pipelines within each model and level; no direction was pre-specified for them. The cached-input sensitivity bills input tokens that repeat the previous call’s prefix in the same trajectory at a fraction cc of an uncached token (Table 24). The analysis program counted the repeated prefix with the Qwen2.5 tokenizer for both models (its re-reading cached counts are identical for the two models), so Mistral’s cached discounts are understated and its cached ratios favour memory. We therefore exclude Mistral’s cached ratios from every claim; an exact recount needs the recorded prompts and Mistral’s own tokenizer and has not been done. For scale only: multiplying Mistral’s cached counts by its re-reading token ratio to Qwen at XL (1.06) suggests that the error could move Mistral’s local repair from below to above full re-reading at c=0.1c=0.1; this is a rough approximation, not a correction, and nothing in the paper relies on it. Table 24 reproduces the hashed output except that Mistral’s invalid cached ratios are replaced by dashes; the no-cache column, taken from server usage, is unaffected. The hashed analysis program printed four of the five pre-specified checks under shifted labels (its P1–P4 are the plan’s P1, P3, P4 and P5, under a heading that cites the wrong plan section) and did not compute P2. Neither file was edited; P2 was computed afterwards, with the plan’s wording, from the per-cell values the program wrote (Table 20). Because each level has its own patients, the S-to-M step in P2 is not a paired comparison. The plan’s other endpoints are in Table 25: cumulative ratios at k=1k=1, 5, 10 and 20, strict completion with exact Clopper–Pearson intervals, and the committed endpoint, which is nn of nn in every cell.

Plan-specified subset reports.

The plan also asks for level S on each longer level’s patients and for the one patient in band at M, L and XL. The hashed program, run unchanged on those patient subsets, gave Table 21. Restricting S to a level’s patients moved re-reading’s per-use tokens by at most 35 and the per-use ratios by at most 0.07, so the S-to-XL changes do not come from which patients were in band. On the same patients, the ratios of Qwen’s cache, rebuild and local repair rose from S to M (1.31, 1.86 and 1.86 to 1.45, 2.09 and 2.08) before falling, and on the single patient in band at M, L and XL (program output, not tabulated) they also rose from S to M before falling (local repair 1.81, 2.21, 1.52 and 0.68 at S, M, L and XL); every Mistral ratio fell at each step. Paired on the XL patients, all six model–pipeline ratios fell from S to XL (Qwen 1.30–1.93 to 0.50–0.65; Mistral 1.35–2.04 to 0.14–0.23).

Full results.

Table 22 gives every cell as written by the hashed analysis program, Table 24 the pre-specified cached-input pricing and Table 25 the remaining pre-specified endpoints.

Extraction at the output cap (exploratory).

Not a pre-specified endpoint; the cap criterion is that of App. E. Of the ingest and revise extraction calls of the four memory pipelines, none of the 836 on the original documents stopped at the 2,048-token output cap, and none at M, but 225 of the 520 calls on added documents at L and XL did (Qwen 110 of 260, Mistral 115 of 260; Table 26); the server’s finish reason and a completion count equal to the cap give the same counts in every model–level–pipeline cell. These 520 calls averaged 1,492 completion tokens (cell means 1,393–1,748), against 205–382 for extractions of the original documents; in the held-out run re-reading’s three answers totalled 294–355 completion tokens (Table 4). All 44 extractions that failed to parse after the labelled repair were Mistral’s, on added documents at L and XL; Mistral’s XL cache, rebuild and local repair used 31–37 % of Qwen’s tokens per use (Table 22), and 38–43 % at L, where only 9 extractions failed to parse, so parse failures alone do not explain the difference. A complete extraction would have produced more ingest output and more rendered claims, so the break-evens at L and XL probably favour memory; this net effect, including any change in summary length, was not measured. A truncated or unparsed extraction admits fewer claims, so part of the memory pipelines’ per-use saving at L and XL reflects content that never entered memory. The added documents carry no medication order and support no expected answer, so the medication endpoints do not depend on them; a task that used them would.

Appendix P Development-stage supplement: one 32B model (EXP-L1, EXP-L2, EXP-L3)

The supplement was run after the 7B results were known, under a pre-specification plan (hashed before any model call under it) and the same frozen build, with the same prompts, scenarios, pipelines and decoding as in Table 5. The model is Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (bf16) (Yang et al., 2024), served by vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023) on one 80–96 GB data-centre GPU per job. A serving check (the extraction prompt on one development document, strict JSON parse, byte-identical greedy replay) preceded the batch and is not a result. One job, 3,140 GPU-seconds; the eight development screening patients ×\times 2 sizes ×\times 4 pipelines = 64 E1 trajectories with two later uses as in Table 5; 0 execution failures. Hardware amendment (dated before the first 32B call): the plan named an 80 GB accelerator; site routing placed the single-GPU job on a 96 GB accelerator of the same class, with model, dtype, context length and decoding unchanged. Counts are descriptive means over development patients; no test was pre-specified and the run is a third model column, not a replicate. Stale commits were 0/8 and strict completion 7/8 in all eight cells; every memory pipeline’s later-use tokens exceeded re-reading’s in all six memory cells (Table 27). The revocation batch (L2) and the replacement batch (L3) of the same plan are reported below.

Replacement with the 32B model (EXP-L3).

Development-stage supplement, not a held-out replication: run after the 7B results of batches C and C2 were known, under the same pre-specification plan and frozen build, with the frozen batch-C and C2 scenario files, the five batch-C pipelines and the frozen field-level scorer. Three cells, never pooled, each disclosing its reuse of patients: dev13 = the 13 batch-C development patients (earlier model runs on these records: batches C and E for all 13 and batches A and B for 7 of them; the third run with this replacement design); calib8 = the 8 calibration patients of C2 stratum A (second use); sealed11 = the 11 sealed patients of C2 stratum B (third use). One 80–96 GB data-centre GPU per cell, 1,859, 1,259 and 1,811 GPU-seconds; 65 + 40 + 55 = 160 trajectories, 0 execution failures. Execution amendment (dated before the jobs started): the batch was first submitted as one job (default queue), cancelled before starting when the scheduler gave no start estimate, and resubmitted unchanged as one job per cell to a short-job queue. Per cell, the one-sided exact test of re-reading >> local repair on adoption (the C2 primary): dev13 discordant 9/0, p=0.0020p=0.0020 (rejected at α=0.05\alpha=0.05); calib8 4/0, p=0.0625p=0.0625 (not rejected; at n=8n=8 rejection needs five or more discordant pairs all on one side, or an 8-pair 7:1 split); sealed11 5/0, p=0.031p=0.031 (rejected). A post-hoc Holm-3 correction across the three cells leaves only dev13 rejected (adjusted p=0.006p=0.006, 0.0625, 0.0625). Smallest Holm-3 adjusted secondary pp: 0.0015, 0.094, 0.094. No-propagation kept the superseded value in 3/13, 4/8 and 4/11. Every non-adoption again occurred with the new value visible in the use prompt; no mechanism attribution is made. Table 28 gives the per-cell counts.

Revocation with the 32B model (EXP-L2).

Development-stage supplement, not a held-out replication: the held-out design of §6.1 (E0, E1, E1b, E4; small size; re-read, cache, rebuild, local repair) run with Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct after the 7B results were known, under the same pre-specification plan and frozen build, graded by the frozen medication grade recorded at run time. Two strata, never pooled, each disclosing its reuse of patients: A = 6 calibration patients never used by any model run before (scenarios generated with the frozen builder, seed 20260918; only six generic-eligible calibration patients remained after the C2 run, so the pre-specified stratum is small and its interval, not its pp-value, is the informative summary); B = the 20 sealed patients of the held-out run, all reused: counting batches in order of completion, this was the fourth evaluation batch for 11 of them (held-out run, C2 stratum B, the L3 sealed cell, then L2) and the second for the other 9 (held-out run, then L2); scenario files byte-identical to the held-out run’s. One 80–96 GB data-centre GPU per condition, each covering both strata, 1,849, 2,505, 2,479 and 2,020 GPU-seconds (8,853 in total); 26 patients ×\times 4 conditions ×\times 4 pipelines = 416 trajectories, 0 execution failures. Execution amendment (dated before the resubmission): the batch was first submitted as one job, cancelled before start when the scheduler gave no start estimate, and split by condition into four jobs; those four failed after about 200 seconds each (813 GPU-seconds, no model output for any scenario) because of a launcher path error; the launcher was corrected, the build, scenarios, clients and decoding were unchanged and re-verified, and the four jobs were resubmitted. Results (Table 29): stale commits 0 in all eight E1 cells (stale is not defined in E0, E1b or E4); the still-supported drug retained in 6/6 in every stratum-A cell and 20/20 in every stratum-B cell except the cache (19/20); the non-allowed E4 drug listed by no pipeline in stratum A and by rebuild and local repair in 1/20 each in stratum B (re-reading and cache 0/20; one-sided exact McNemar p=0.5p=0.5 for each, p=1p=1 for the cache); strict completion 6/6 (re-reading) and 5/6 (memory pipelines) in stratum A and 16–18/20 in stratum B; re-reading cheapest in every cell.
